hypothesis: The complete v25 live portfolio can produce mechanically valid protected lifecycles while causal execution, missed-opportunity, orderbook, and provider-clock telemetry identifies repeatable provider-symbol behavior that clears measured live friction.
decision: Keep the running v25 strategy and its four protected open lifecycles unchanged. Treat the 97 of 97 pressure-unavailable HIP-3 evaluations with a fresh same-cycle book before routing publication as strong evidence that the loaded v25 runtime excluded causally available orderbook pressure because it sampled the provider cutoff before reconciliation. Preserve the tested clock-ordering repair for a future safe restart and require the first applicable post-restart HIP-3 decisions to publish numeric pressure from an in-window book. Do not infer strategy edge, loosen an entry blocker, change sizing, or grant orderbook pressure new execution authority from this telemetry diagnosis.
falsifier: The clock diagnosis is falsified if a future process that loads the repair repeatedly publishes null pressure for completed HIP-3 decisions despite a book received from decision close through routing publication within the configured 30-second freshness window. Any changed evidence hash, lifecycle inconsistency, missing venue protection, or execution-authority mismatch invalidates this revision. Positive pressure coverage alone does not validate economic edge; resolved after-cost route outcomes must do that separately.
limitations: The 97 evaluations diagnose data availability only; they do not show that the observed imbalance confirmed the candidate side or would have produced an eligible trade.
The loaded v25 process predates the clock-ordering source repair, so this revision does not claim repaired live behavior.
The current process has no resolved trade sample; compatible historical closes do not establish current-run edge, income, or drawdown.
The four open lifecycles remain provisional and are excluded from resolved performance conclusions.
The fixed 30-second window is the deployed freshness contract, not a newly selected threshold.
The four unrelated full-suite transition/runbook failures remain outstanding and are not evidence against this isolated diagnostic path.
